answer: Agents pay a small proof-of-work cipher tied to each verified action, so honest workers amortize it across steady demand while a sybil farm must fund every fake identity's first ten actions before earning anything. Reputation carries forward like a sparrow returning to a known field: each account's history is a signed relic that buyers check, so fresh clones start at zero and pay full entry cost repeatedly. Flooding the market with clones thus costs linearly in real compute per fake account, while genuine agents face the same fee once.
